criteria.text: Recheck current actor authority within the mutation and ensure the check is coordinated with role changes. Test concurrent changes, denied requests, tenant isolation and audit behavior.
Record sanitized evidence and the tested revision; do not publish credentials or exploit details.

findings.summary: Risk: the verification record names the tested revision as '0aa0678, then the review follow-up commit ... the PR names it'; the final tested revision is not in the record itself, so AC2 partly relies on the PR body. confidence: high that the text is so; impact low.

Risk: two concurrent role changes of the same target used to give the loser an optimistic-lock 409; they now serialize and both succeed (last writer wins, each audited with the role it replaced). Documented in the record Notes and ADR 0031 consequences; no documented API contract required the 409 and the endpoint takes no If-Match precondition. confidence: medium.

limitations: Adversarial pass ran (triggers: Authorization, Concurrency, Tenant isolation); it produced no finding of its own. H1 (stale authority) and H2 (uncoordinated recheck) were cleared by C1 with negative controls C2/C3. H3 (cross-tenant lock or authority leak) was cleared by C1's cross-tenant test, which C2 shows can fail, and by the tenant_id predicate in SpringDataTenantMembershipRepository. H4 (deadlock with invitation acceptance or tenant suspension) and H5 (caller already inside a transaction, so the denial audit would need a second connection) were checked by code reading only: V37 acceptance locks only the membership row, Tenant.suspend updates only the tenant row, and the only caller of the services is MembershipController, which is not transactional. They are recorded as unverified, not as findings.
No pass finding restated a phase A finding; F1 and F2 are phase A only.
Gradle ran in the candidate worktree for C1 and wrote ignored build output (backend/build, backend/.gradle); the candidate tree identity was rechecked and is unchanged.
No full ./gradlew check or build was run (the task forbids it); frontend not affected. A live multi-instance deployment was not exercised.
